newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot electricity firm on cold front.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot electricity firm on cold front.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the southeast U.S. firmed Wednesday on outlook of a cold front beginning to move into the region as early as Thursday, market sources said.
"Kentucky is expected to have pretty cold weather," said a Southeast trader.
According to Weather Services Corp's latest forecast, a cold, dry weather system could bring temperatures six to 12 Fahrenheit degrees below normal into the Southeast through the middle of next week.
Tighter generating capacity due to plant outages in the northwestern outskirt of Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) service region also bolstered prices, market sources said.
In the northwestern part of TVA's territory, firm, peak power for Thursday delivery was quoted at $18.00-$19.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), up from Tuesday's $17.00-$18.00.
Firm, next-day power for delivery into northwestern TVA during light load hours on Thursday was still assessed at $12.00-$14.00.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity for Thursday delivery held steady in the $21.00-$22.50 area.
Firm, off-peak power for Thursday at the Ga./Fla. border was again valued in the $15.00-$17.00 range.
TVA was again heard offering next-day, non-firm electricity for peak hours at $21.50, and for off-peak hours at $17.00. Market sources noted TVA spot power supply was limited, and was sold out early.
TVA restored its 1,148 MW Sequoyah nuclear unit 2 in Soddy Daisy, Tenn., to full output late Tuesday following its refueling outage that began October 11.
